name: Champion Iron Limited
executive_summary: Champion Iron Limited (CIA.AX) is a Quebec-focused producer of high-grade iron ore concentrate at Bloom Lake, pivoting toward direct-reduction pellet feed (DRPF) and green-steel end markets, with the Kami project and Rana Gruber acquisition extending the growth pipeline. The quantitative screen rates the name a **buy** (9/22 models, composite 61%; P/E 12.0, P/B 1.4, yield 3.2%, current ratio 2.60). The valuation hook is a profitable, dividend-paying operator on modest multiples while funding a structurally higher-margin product mix. The central debate is whether DRPF commissioning, destocking of ~2.6M wmt of concentrate inventory, and M&A can lift earnings above the FY2024 peak, or whether iron ore cyclicality, rising leverage, and a dividend reset will cap returns despite attractive headline metrics. FY2026 primary filings are absent from the library; FY2025 annual and Q4 bodies support the operational story but not full-year audited P&L detail.
investment_thesis:
For a value investor, CIA.AX combines Graham-style defensibility with a visible growth option. The screen passes nine models across cheapness, dividend, GARP, and risk families — including Graham Defensive, Graham Enterprising, Earnings Yield, Neff PEGY, Dividend Growth, Magic Formula, Acquirer's Multiple, Dreman Contrarian, and Financial Health — suggesting the market is not fully pricing a business that remains cash-generative through the cycle.

Business quality rests on Bloom Lake: 15M wmt/year nameplate capacity, 66%+ Fe concentrate, hydro-powered operations, and a premium to benchmark indices. Management is deliberately moving upmarket — DRPF commissioning targeted December 2025 (per FY2025 filings), DR-quality commercial production announced June 2026 (news), and the Rana Gruber deal (90% acceptance, March 2026) diversifies geography and green-steel exposure. Record Q3 FY2026 production and National Bank initiation (June 2026) support the operational narrative.

The screen’s negative trailing FCF figure (approximately –C$19.4M) reflects heavy investment: Yahoo annual data shows FY2026 operating cash flow of C$436M against capex of C$414M, yielding modest positive FCF of C$22M — an inflection from FY2025’s –C$302M. At P/E 12.0 and ROE 11.4%, the market appears to discount execution risk on capex and M&A rather than imminent distress. Screen conviction is moderate (46%, four weeks at signal, stable), supporting an accumulate stance rather than high-conviction buy.
financial_review:
**Primary sources used:** Annual Information Form (AIF) for the year ended 31 March 2025 (29 May 2025); FY2025 Q4 results press release (29 May 2025). **Gap:** No FY2026 annual AIF, MD&A, or Q4 results body is indexed; full-year consolidated trends below fall back to **`financials_annual.json` (Yahoo Finance)** where filing bodies lack audited group figures.

### Annual / operational (AIF, FY2025)

Bloom Lake produced **13.8M wmt** of 66.4% Fe concentrate in FY2025 (AIF). Concentrate stockpiled at site totalled **2.6M wmt** at 31 March 2025, with management expecting continued destocking as rail capacity improves (AIF; corroborated in Q4 release). DRPF capital deployed in FY2025 was **C$244.3M**, cumulative **C$339.5M** of an estimated **C$470.7M** total project cost (AIF). Proven and probable reserves stood at **636 Mt** at 28.6% Fe, with a **15-year** life-of-mine (AIF).

Financing structure (AIF): US$400M revolving credit facility extended to November 2027; US$230M term facility maturing November 2028, with documents including “standard and customary finance terms and conditions, including with respect to fees, representations, warranties, **covenants** and conditions precedent.” Specific covenant thresholds are not reproduced in the available body extract; the 2025 MD&A (referenced but not downloaded) would be required for detail. Dividend policy through FY2025: **C$0.10 per share semi-annually** — an eighth consecutive declaration on 28 May 2025 (AIF).

### Interim / Q4 FY2025 (filing body, quarter ended 31 March 2025)

| Metric | Q4 FY25 | Q4 FY24 | YoY |

| EBITDA | C$127.4M | C$85.1M | +50% |
| Net income | C$39.1M | C$25.8M | +52% |
| EPS | C$0.08 | C$0.05 | +60% |

| C1 cash cost | C$80.0/dmt | C$76.6/dmt | +4% |
| Net realised price | US$84.9/dmt | — | +2% YoY (per release) |

Cash at 31 March 2025: **C$117.5M**; available liquidity (cash plus undrawn credit): **C$605.9M** (Q4 release). Stockpile reduced by 341,000 wmt in the quarter to 2.6M wmt. EBITDA margin reached **30%** versus 26% in Q4 FY24.

### Full-year trend (Yahoo fallback — audited FY2025/FY2026 group P&L not in filing bodies)

| Metric | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 | FY2026 |
|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|
| Revenue | C$1,395M | C$1,524M | C$1,607M | C$1,770M |
| Net income | C$201M | C$234M | C$142M | C$169M |
| Basic EPS | C$0.39 | C$0.45 | C$0.27 | C$0.32 |
| EBITDA | C$482M | C$555M | C$446M | C$508M |

Revenue grew **+27%** over four years; earnings are cyclical — FY2024 peak net income **C$234M** compressed **39%** in FY2025 before partial recovery in FY2026 (**C$169M**), still **28%** below the peak. FY2026 net income includes **C$16.7M** in securities gains (Yahoo unusual items); normalised income **C$159M**.

**Balance sheet (Yahoo, FY2026):** Total assets C$3,497M; equity C$1,534M; cash C$297M; total debt C$1,081M; **net debt C$666M** (versus C$121M in FY2023). Current ratio ~**2.60** (screen-consistent). Construction in progress C$561M; long-term provisions C$132M. Interest expense C$43M on EBIT C$328M → coverage ~**7.7×** (down from ~11× in FY2024).

**Cash flow (Yahoo):** Operating cash flow C$436M (FY2026); capex –C$414M; **FCF C$22M** (versus –C$302M in FY2025). Dividends paid C$103–107M annually through the cycle — consuming most FY2026 FCF.

**Interim gap:** FY2026 Q4 results (reported late May 2026 per news) and any FY2026 AIF/MD&A are **not indexed** with downloadable bodies. Going-concern assessments, rehabilitation provisions, tax contingencies, and detailed covenant compliance **cannot be verified** from primary sources for the current year.
risks_and_flags:
**Commodity cyclicality.** The AIF lists iron ore prices, steel demand, freight costs, and global economic conditions among principal risks; FY2025 earnings fell sharply despite volume growth, demonstrating operating leverage. Q4 FY25 release notes freight disruption via the Cape of Good Hope and provisional pricing sensitivity.

**Infrastructure and logistics dependence.** AIF risk factors highlight reliance on third-party rail (QNS&L) and port infrastructure; Bloom Lake stockpiles reached 2.6M wmt when rail lagged production. Q4 FY25 cites seasonal weather, semi-annual plant shutdowns, and ore-hardness-related grinding wear as ongoing cost pressures.

**Liquidity / financing and covenants.** Credit facilities (US$630M combined) carry covenant language per the AIF, but thresholds are not in the available extract. Net debt has risen sixfold from FY2024 to FY2026 (Yahoo). DRPF remaining capex (~C$130M on AIF estimates) and Rana Gruber integration add further funding needs. **No going-concern qualification** appears in available filing bodies; this is not confirmation of absence in unaudited MD&A text.

**Single-asset and execution concentration.** AIF explicitly flags dependence on Bloom Lake and development/expansion project risks. DRPF commissioning timing and Kami partnership execution (Nippon/Sojitz binding agreement, December 2024) remain forward-looking.

**Environmental and social.** Land reclamation, mine closure costs, First Nations land claims, water management, and carbon policy (including structural shift to EAF/DRI steelmaking) are enumerated in the AIF risk register. Long-term provisions C$132M (Yahoo) cannot be reconciled to filing rehabilitation schedules without MD&A.

**Dividend reset.** Multiple news items (May–July 2026) reference a lower dividend and capital-priority recalibration — e.g. *Champion Iron Shares Lag ASX Today: Dividend Cut In Framework Shift* (29 May 2026). This challenges the screen’s dividend-family pass even as a reduced dividend was declared for the six months ended 31 March 2026 (payable 8 July 2026).

**Governance transition.** CFO Michael Marcotte and Chief Legal & Strategy Officer Steve Boucratie appointed 16 July 2026 — leadership change during a capex/M&A cycle warrants monitoring; no adverse context in available sources.

**Earnings quality.** Securities gains/losses (C$16.7M gain FY2026; C$17.5M loss FY2025 per Yahoo) add volatility. Latest Yahoo quarterly net income C$23M (FY2026 Q4 cache) is well below record Q3 levels cited in news.

**Capital markets**

**Corporate actions**
- *Champion Iron Shares Lag ASX Today: Dividend Cut In Framework Shift* (29 May 2026): Material for income investors.
- *Champion Iron Limited Announces Actual Ordinary Fully Paid Dividend for the Six Months Ended March 31, 2026, Payable on July 8, 2026* (2 July 2026).
- *Champion Iron Limited Announces Appointment of Michael Marcotte as Chief Financial Officer* (16 July 2026); *…Steve Boucratie as Chief Legal & Strategy Officer and Corporate Secretary* (16 July 2026).

No material adverse regulatory actions appear in the manifest. Coverage is adequate for strategic tracking but thin on covenant detail, environmental liabilities, and indigenous consultation.
research_rationale: Primary FY2025 filings confirm operational momentum, liquidity headroom, and a coherent growth strategy, broadly supporting the screen’s cheapness case, but rising leverage, a dividend reset, missing FY2026 filing bodies, and unproven DRPF/M&A returns prevent full confirmation of the quantitative buy signal.
